native_context: Windows service configuration and file authority
taxonomy_note: Planning lens only; actual root-cause mapping is independent.

controls.boundary: Windows service configuration and file authority — authoritative consumer
controls.source_trace: Collect the low-privilege token/groups, service DACL/configuration, service account, executable/argument path and file/parent ACLs. Record the trigger that makes the service consume a change.
controls.controlled_verification: Use read-only effective-access inspection or an inert owned replica. Determine whether the alleged actor can change the exact service setting or consumed file/path and whether a privileged service will actually use it under the stated trigger. Do not replace a real service binary or restart production for proof.
controls.false_positive_discriminator: An unquoted path or readable executable alone is not escalation. The actor needs control of a viable consumed path/configuration; permissions on one directory may not apply to the relevant object.
controls.remediation_acceptance: Remove the specific unintended edit authority at the service/file/parent boundary while preserving intended operators. Re-evaluate the low-privilege token and valid maintenance workflow.

coverage_unit: One primary investigative assertion for this technique; not exhaustive coverage. Expand only for genuinely distinct policy/effect assertions in the actual assessment.
